records.source: Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ, εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ.
records.gloss: When he had completed all the words of him in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
pieces: When Jesus had finished saying all these things to the people who were listening, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into Capernaum.

L.1: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had completed all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words in the hearing of the people, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered into Capernaum.

R.1: Jesus finished teaching the people. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went to the town of Capernaum.

decisions.choice: all his words: the teaching of 6:20-49
decisions.reason: The sentence closes the sermon of chapter 6 and moves to a new scene. "In the hearing of the people" recalls that the crowd, not only the disciples, heard it (6:17-19).

decisions.choice: Capernaum: a town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Jesus made the town a base for his work in Galilee (4:31).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

records.heading: A centurion's servant is healed

records.source: Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος.
records.gloss: Of a centurion then a certain slave being ill was about to die, who was to him highly valued.
pieces: There was a centurion whose servant was very dear to him, and the servant was ill and close to death.

L.2: Now a certain centurion's slave, who was highly valued by him, was sick and about to die.

R.2: An army officer called a centurion lived there. He had a servant whom he valued very much. The servant was sick and about to die.

decisions.choice: centurion: an army officer in command of about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: The title means the commander of a hundred. Galilee was ruled by Herod Antipas (3:1), whose troops were organized in the Roman way. The centurion was a Gentile, not a Jew: the Jewish elders speak of "our nation" as if it were not his (7:5).

decisions.choice: slave: a person who belonged to his master
decisions.reason: The word is the usual word for a slave, as in 2:29. The slave was his master's property, not a paid worker. In 7:7 the centurion calls him by another word, see the note there.

decisions.choice: highly valued: dear to his master, and also of great worth to him
decisions.reason: The word means held in honor or prized. It can describe something precious (1 Peter 2:4, 6). The centurion's concern shows that the slave mattered to him as a person.

decisions.choice: an army officer called a centurion lived there
decisions.reason: Readable says what a centurion was, and places him in Capernaum, as 7:1 implies.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρεσβυτέρους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐρωτῶν αὐτὸν ὅπως ἐλθὼν διασώσῃ τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Having heard then about Jesus he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him that having come he might save the slave of him.
pieces: He heard about Jesus and sent some Jewish elders to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come and save his servant's life.

L.3: And having heard about Jesus, he sent to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} elders of the Jews, asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come and save his slave.

R.3: The centurion heard about Jesus. So he sent some leaders of the Jews to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He wanted them to ask Jesus to come and make his servant well.

decisions.choice: elders of the Jews: respected older men who led the Jewish community of the town
alternatives: members of the ruling council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Each Jewish town had its elders, who settled local matters and led the synagogue community. The centurion does not come himself but sends men whom Jesus, a Jew, would trust.

decisions.choice: save: bring safely through, here from death
decisions.reason: The verb means to rescue someone all the way through a danger. The slave is about to die (7:2), and the request is that his life be saved.

decisions.choice: his slave: the same word as in 7:2
decisions.reason: Luke keeps the word for slave in 7:2, 3, 8 and 10.

decisions.choice: make his servant well
decisions.reason: Readable says what saving the servant meant here: healing him before he died.

decisions.choice: leaders of the Jews
decisions.reason: Today "elders" suggests only age or a church office. Readable says what they were.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m3) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν σπουδαίως λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄξιός ἐστιν ᾧ παρέξῃ τοῦτο, ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν.
records.gloss: And having come to Jesus they were begging him earnestly saying that, Worthy he is for whom you will grant this, \v 5 he loves for the nation of us and the synagogue he built for us.
pieces: They came to Jesus and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} urgently. "He deserves to have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do this for him," they said.
"He loves our people, and he is the one who built our synagogue for us."

L.4: And when they came to Jesus, they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} earnestly, saying, "He is worthy for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to grant this to him,
L.5: for he loves our nation, and he himself built the synagogue for us."

R.4: They came to Jesus and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to help. They said, "This man deserves {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help.
R.5: He loves our people, and he even paid to build our synagogue."

decisions.choice: worthy: deserving, because of what he has done
decisions.reason: The elders argue from the centurion's good deeds. In 7:6-7 the centurion says the opposite of himself: he is not worthy. The two words come from the same root.

decisions.choice: he loves our nation and built our synagogue: a Gentile friendly to the Jews and their worship
decisions.reason: Some Gentiles honored the God of Israel and supported the synagogue without becoming Jews, like Cornelius, another centurion (Acts 10:1-2, 22). The elders do not say he had become a Jew.

decisions.choice: he himself built: he paid for the building
alternatives: he built it with his own hands
decisions.reason: The pronoun stresses that it was his gift. A wealthy patron "built" by paying for the work.

decisions.choice: the request in two sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the elders' words into shorter sentences.

decisions.choice: paid to build
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the centurion paid for the building, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐπορεύετο σὺν αὐτοῖς.
records.gloss: And Jesus was going with them.
pieces: So Jesus went with them.

L.6: And Jesus was going with them.

decisions.choice: was going: Jesus was on his way
decisions.reason: The tense describes the journey under way. Before Jesus reaches the house, the centurion sends a second message (7:6).

records.source: ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἔπεμψεν φίλους ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης λέγων αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μὴ σκύλλου, οὐ γὰρ ἱκανός εἰμι ἵνα ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην μου εἰσέλθῃς·
records.gloss: Already then him not far being distant from the house sent friends the centurion saying to him, Lord, not trouble yourself, not for worthy I am that under the roof of me you should come;
pieces: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, do not put {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} to any trouble. I am not worthy to have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come under my roof.

L.6: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was already not far from the house, the centurion sent friends, saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, do not trouble {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, for I am not worthy for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to come under my roof;

R.6: Jesus was getting close to the house when the centurion sent some friends with a message for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, do not trouble {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}. I am not good enough to have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come into my house.

decisions.choice: Lord: a title of respect that, in Luke's telling, says more than "sir"
decisions.reason: The word can be a polite address. But the centurion speaks of Jesus's word as having power to command a sickness (7:7-8). Luke's readers hear the title he uses for God and for Jesus (2:11).

decisions.choice: come under my roof: enter my house
alternatives: a fear of being made unclean himself
decisions.reason: Devout Jews avoided entering a Gentile's house, because it would make them ritually unclean (Acts 10:28; 11:2-3). The centurion knows this, but he also speaks of his own unworthiness: he will not ask Jesus to come.

decisions.choice: trouble yourself: put yourself to effort, be bothered
decisions.reason: The verb first meant to harass or wear out. Here it is a courteous phrase: do not go to the trouble.

decisions.choice: saying to him: the friends speak the centurion's words
alternatives: the centurion came and spoke himself
decisions.reason: The centurion speaks through his friends, as he first spoke through the elders (7:3). Matthew tells the story more briefly, as if the centurion spoke in person (Matthew 8:5-13).

decisions.choice: I am not good enough to have you come into my house
alternatives: I am not worthy that you should come under my roof
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of the roof.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:8
alternatives: a separate quotation in each verse
decisions.reason: The centurion's message runs on through 7:7-8 as one speech.

records.source: διὸ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἠξίωσα πρὸς σὲ ἐλθεῖν· ἀλλὰ εἰπὲ λόγῳ, καὶ ἰαθήτω ὁ παῖς μου·
records.gloss: Therefore neither myself I considered worthy to you to come; but say in a word, and let be healed the servant of me.
pieces: That is why I did not think myself fit to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} myself. Only speak a command, and let my servant be healed.

L.7: Therefore neither did I consider myself worthy to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; but say with a word, and let my servant be healed.

R.7: That is why I did not come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} myself. Just give the order, and my servant will be well.

decisions.choice: servant: the same slave as in 7:2, called by a word of the household
decisions.reason: The word can mean a child, a boy, or a slave of any age; masters often called a household slave "boy". Luke has already said that the sick man is a slave (7:2, 3) and will say so again (7:10), so here it is not a son. The centurion uses the warmer household word, which matches how dear the slave was to him.

decisions.choice: say with a word: give a command, without coming
decisions.reason: The centurion believes Jesus's spoken order is enough, even at a distance. The following verse explains why.

decisions.choice: let him be healed: a command form, confident of the result
alternatives: a wish: may he be healed
decisions.reason: The form is an imperative. The centurion speaks of the healing as sure to follow the command.

decisions.choice: let him be healed, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: he will be healed, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts have the command form; many others have the future, as in Matthew 8:8. The meaning is close either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: A different Greek word from the one in 7:2, which Literal renders "slave"; Balanced and Readable have "servant" for both, since the same man is meant. "Boy" would suggest a child, which Luke's other verses rule out.

decisions.choice: Just give the order
decisions.reason: Readable says what speaking a word means here.

records.source: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος, ἔχων ὑπ’ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ· Πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ· Ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου· Ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.
records.gloss: Also for I a man am under authority being placed, having under myself soldiers, and I say to this one, Go, and he goes, and to another, Come, and he comes, and to the slave of me, Do this, and he does.
pieces: For I myself serve under men who have authority over me, and I have soldiers under my command. I say to one, 'Go!' and off he goes; to another, 'Come here!' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this!' and he does it."

L.8: For I also am a man placed under authority, having soldiers under me, and I say to this one, 'Go,' and he goes, and to another, 'Come,' and he comes, and to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does [it]."

R.8: I know about giving orders. I have officers over me, and I have soldiers who obey me. I tell one soldier, 'Go!' and he goes. I tell another, 'Come here!' and he comes. I tell my servant, 'Do this!' and he does it."

decisions.choice: I also am under authority: like Jesus, he stands in a chain of command
alternatives: I am a man of authority
decisions.reason: The centurion reasons from his own life. He obeys those above him and is obeyed by those below him; his word carries the authority of his superiors. So Jesus's word carries God's authority, and sickness must obey it.

decisions.choice: my slave: a slave of his household
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in 7:2 for a slave. The centurion is not necessarily speaking of the sick man.

decisions.choice: I know about giving orders. I have officers over me
alternatives: I also am a man placed under authority
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the comparison in plain words.

decisions.choice: Come here!
decisions.reason: The command in English needs "here" to sound natural.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν αὐτόν, καὶ στραφεὶς τῷ ἀκολουθοῦντι αὐτῷ ὄχλῳ εἶπεν· Λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον.
records.gloss: Having heard then these things Jesus marveled at him, and having turned to the following him crowd he said, I say to you, not even in the Israel such great faith did I find.
pieces: When Jesus heard this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was amazed at the man. Turning to the crowd that followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I tell you, I have not found faith this great even in Israel."

L.9: And hearing these things, Jesus marveled at him, and turning to the crowd that was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith."

R.9: Jesus was amazed when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard this. He turned to the crowd that was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "I tell you, not even among God's people in Israel have I seen faith as strong as this man's!"

decisions.choice: marveled: was amazed
decisions.reason: The Gospels seldom say that Jesus was amazed. Mark 6:6 says he was amazed at the unbelief in his hometown; here a Gentile's trust amazes him.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Jesus's power and authority to heal by his word
decisions.reason: The centurion's faith is his confidence that Jesus's command will be obeyed (7:7-8). In Luke faith is trust in Jesus shown in action (5:20; 7:50).

decisions.choice: not even in Israel: a Gentile's faith surpasses what Jesus has met among God's own people
decisions.reason: Simeon sang that Jesus would be a light for the Gentiles (2:32). Jesus said that Elijah and Elisha were sent to foreigners (4:25-27).

decisions.choice: among God's people in Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says what Israel means here: the people, not only the land.

decisions.choice: faith as strong as this man's
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key term faith and makes the comparison plain.

records.source: καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον οἱ πεμφθέντες εὗρον τὸν δοῦλον ὑγιαίνοντα.
records.gloss: And having returned to the house those having been sent found the slave in good health.
pieces: When the messengers went back to the house, they found the servant well.

L.10: And when those who had been sent returned to the house, they found the slave in good health.

R.10: The men who had been sent went back to the centurion's house. They found that the servant was well again.

decisions.choice: in good health: fully healthy
decisions.reason: The word means sound and healthy (5:31). The slave who was about to die (7:2) is now well; Jesus never went to the house.

decisions.choice: those who had been sent: the friends of 7:6, and perhaps the elders too
decisions.reason: Luke does not say exactly who; it is the centurion's messengers.

decisions.choice: the centurion's house
decisions.reason: Readable says whose house it was.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν, καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς.
records.gloss: And it came about in the next [time] he went into a town being called Nain, and were going with him the disciples of him and a crowd great.
pieces: Soon afterward Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and so did a large crowd.

L.11: And it happened soon afterward [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went to a town called Nain, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and a large crowd were going with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

R.11: Soon after this Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and a large crowd of people followed too.

decisions.choice: soon afterward, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: on the next day, the reading of other manuscripts
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has a form that means "in the time following". Other manuscripts have a form that means "on the next day". The two differ by one letter. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Nain: a village in southern Galilee
decisions.reason: The Bible mentions Nain only here. It lay a few miles southeast of Nazareth, near the village of Shunem, where Elisha raised a woman's son (2 Kings 4:8-37).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

records.heading: The widow's son at Nain

records.source: ὡς δὲ ἤγγισεν τῇ πύλῃ τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξεκομίζετο τεθνηκὼς μονογενὴς υἱὸς τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὴ ἦν χήρα, καὶ ὄχλος τῆς πόλεως ἱκανὸς ἦν σὺν αὐτῇ.
records.gloss: As then he drew near to the gate of the town, and look was being carried out having died an only son of the mother of him, and she was a widow, and a crowd of the town considerable was with her.
pieces: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came near the town gate, a dead man was being carried out. He was his mother's only son, and she was a widow. A large crowd from the town was with her.

L.12: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came near the gate of the town, look, a man who had died was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a considerable crowd from the town was with her.

R.12: As Jesus came near the gate of the town, some people were carrying out a dead man to bury him. He was the only son of his mother, and her husband had died. Many people from the town were with her.

decisions.choice: being carried out: taken out of the town for burial
decisions.reason: Burials took place outside towns, usually on the day of death. The body was carried on an open frame, with the family and mourners following.

decisions.choice: only: the one and only son
decisions.reason: The word means the only one of its kind (8:42; 9:38). Luke uses it of an only child.

decisions.choice: a widow: a woman whose husband has died, now without her son as well
alternatives: a woman living alone by choice
decisions.reason: With no husband and no son, she had lost those who would provide for and protect her. The law tells God's people to care for widows (Deuteronomy 24:17-21).

decisions.choice: a widow's only son: the story recalls Elijah at Zarephath
decisions.reason: Elijah met a widow at the town gate and raised her son (1 Kings 17:10, 17-24). Jesus has already pointed to that widow (4:25-26). 7:15 uses the words of 1 Kings 17:23.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: to bury him
decisions.reason: Readable says why the body was being carried out.

decisions.choice: her husband had died
decisions.reason: Readable says what being a widow means.

records.source: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν ὁ κύριος ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτῇ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μὴ κλαῖε.
records.gloss: And having seen her the Lord felt compassion on her and said to her, Not weep.
pieces: When the Lord saw her, pity for her moved {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} deeply, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "Stop weeping."

L.13: And seeing her, the Lord had compassion on her and said to her, "Do not weep."

R.13: When the Lord Jesus saw her, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} felt very sorry for her. He said to her, "Do not cry."

decisions.choice: the Lord: Luke the narrator calls Jesus by the title used for God
decisions.reason: This is the first time Luke himself, telling the story, calls Jesus "the Lord". The angels announced him as Christ the Lord (2:11); Luke uses the title often from now on (7:19; 10:1).

decisions.choice: had compassion: felt a deep, inward pity that moves to action
alternatives: felt sorry in a distant way
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for the inner parts of the body, thought of as the seat of feeling (1:78). Luke uses it of the Samaritan (10:33) and the father of the lost son (15:20).

decisions.choice: do not weep: stop weeping
decisions.reason: The form tells someone to stop what they are already doing.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name so that a new reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: pity for her moved him deeply
alternatives: his heart went out to her
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the depth of the feeling in its own words.

records.source: καὶ προσελθὼν ἥψατο τῆς σοροῦ, οἱ δὲ βαστάζοντες ἔστησαν, καὶ εἶπεν· Νεανίσκε, σοὶ λέγω, ἐγέρθητι.
records.gloss: And having come near he touched the bier, those then carrying stood still, and he said, Young man, to you I say, arise.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up and touched the bier, and the men carrying it stood still. He said, "Young man, I tell you, get up!"

L.14: And coming near, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched the bier, and those carrying [it] stood still, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Young man, I say to you, arise."

R.14: Then Jesus went up and touched the frame they were carrying the body on. The men carrying it stopped. Jesus said, "Young man, I tell you, get up!"

decisions.choice: bier: the open frame or stretcher on which the body was carried
decisions.reason: Jewish burials did not use closed coffins; the body, wrapped in cloth, lay on an open bier. Touching it would make a person unclean under the law (Numbers 19:11-16), but Jesus's touch brings life.

decisions.choice: arise: get up, be raised
decisions.reason: The verb is used of getting up and of being raised from the dead (7:22; 9:22).

decisions.choice: to you I say: Jesus commands by his own authority
decisions.reason: Elijah and Elisha prayed to the LORD before the dead were raised (1 Kings 17:20-21; 2 Kings 4:33). Jesus speaks directly to the dead man.

decisions.choice: the frame they were carrying the body on
decisions.reason: "Bier" is a rare word, and "coffin" would be wrong.

records.source: καὶ ἀνεκάθισεν ὁ νεκρὸς καὶ ἤρξατο λαλεῖν, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And sat up the dead [man] and began to speak, and he gave him to the mother of him.
pieces: The dead man sat up and began to talk, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.

L.15: And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him to his mother.

R.15: The dead man sat up and began to talk! And Jesus gave him back to his mother.

decisions.choice: he gave him to his mother: the words of 1 Kings 17:23
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses the same words of Elijah, who gave the widow's son back to his mother. The people's response in 7:16 names Jesus a great prophet.

decisions.choice: began to speak: proof that he was truly alive
decisions.reason: Luke does not tell what he said; his speaking shows that life has returned.

decisions.choice: Jesus gave him back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since several men have been mentioned, and say "back" because she had lost him.

records.source: ἔλαβεν δὲ φόβος πάντας, καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν λέγοντες ὅτι Προφήτης μέγας ἠγέρθη ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅτι Ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Seized then fear all, and they were glorifying the God saying that, A prophet great has been raised among us, and that, Has visited the God the people of him.
pieces: Awe took hold of everyone, and they gave glory to God. "A great prophet has appeared among us!" they said, and, "God has come to help {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people!"

L.16: And fear seized [them] all, and they were glorifying God, saying, "A great prophet has been raised up among us," and, "God has visited {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people!"

R.16: Everyone there was filled with fear and wonder, and they gave glory to God. They said, "A great prophet has come to us!" They also said, "God has come to help {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people!"

decisions.choice: fear: awe before God's power
decisions.reason: As in 5:26, people are filled with fear when God acts among them.

decisions.choice: glorifying God: praising God for what he has done
decisions.reason: People in Luke give glory to God when they see his work (2:20; 5:25-26).

decisions.choice: has been raised up: God has sent a prophet
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 7:14, but here it means that God has caused a prophet to appear, as Moses promised (Deuteronomy 18:15).

decisions.choice: visited: came to help
decisions.reason: As in 1:68 and 1:78, God visits his people when he comes to act for them (Exodus 4:31; Ruth 1:6).

decisions.choice: gave glory to God
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for glory; Balanced and Readable keep that word, as in 5:25.

decisions.choice: has come to help his people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "visited", as in 1:68.

decisions.choice: awe (B); fear and wonder (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:26, "fear" alone would suggest terror.

records.source: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ.
records.gloss: And went out the report this in all the Judea concerning him and all the surrounding region.
pieces: This news about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} spread through all Judea and the whole region around it.

L.17: And this report about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went out in all Judea and all the surrounding region.

R.17: The news about what Jesus had done spread everywhere in the land of the Jews and in all the places around it.

decisions.choice: Judea: the whole land of the Jews
alternatives: only the southern region around Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Nain is in Galilee, so Judea here means the land where the Jews lived, as in 1:5 and 4:44.

decisions.choice: report: the word that was told about him
decisions.reason: The noun is the usual word for word or message; here it is the news that spread by word of mouth.

decisions.choice: the land of the Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains the broad sense of Judea, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: what Jesus had done
decisions.reason: Readable says what the news was about.

records.source: Καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν Ἰωάννῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ περὶ πάντων τούτων.
records.gloss: And reported to John the disciples of him concerning all these things.
pieces: John's disciples told him about all these things.

L.18: And John's disciples reported to him about all these things.

R.18: John's followers told him about everything Jesus was doing.

decisions.choice: John: John the Baptist, now in prison
decisions.reason: Herod had locked John up in prison (3:19-20). His disciples still visited him.

decisions.choice: all these things: Jesus's healings and teaching, including the raising at Nain
decisions.reason: The phrase sums up what Luke has told since John's arrest.

decisions.choice: followers
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for disciples here, since they were not Jesus's disciples.

decisions.choice: everything Jesus was doing
decisions.reason: Readable says what "these things" were.

records.heading: John asks about the one who is to come

records.source: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος δύο τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν κύριον λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;
records.gloss: And having called to [him] two certain of the disciples of him John \v 19 sent to the Lord saying, You are the coming [one] or another should we wait for?
pieces: So John called two of his disciples
and sent them to the Lord to ask, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is to come, or are we to look for someone else?"

L.18: And calling two of his disciples, John
L.19: sent [them] to the Lord, saying, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is coming, or should we wait for another?"

R.18: So John called two of his followers.
R.19: He sent them to the Lord Jesus to ask, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one God promised would come? Or should we keep waiting for someone else?"

decisions.choice: the one who is coming: the one God promised to send
decisions.reason: John had said that one more powerful than he was coming (3:16). The prophets spoke of the LORD's messenger who comes (Malachi 3:1) and of the one who comes in the name of the LORD (Psalm 118:26; Luke 13:35).

decisions.choice: John's question: a real question, not a test for his disciples' sake
alternatives: John is sure and asks only for his disciples
decisions.reason: John had announced one who would judge with fire (3:16-17). Jesus is healing, not judging, and John is in prison. Jesus answers with what he is doing (7:22).

decisions.choice: the Lord, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Jesus, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "Jesus"; several early ones read "the Lord". The person meant is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the one who is to come (B); the one who is coming (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that his coming was promised.

decisions.choice: the one God promised would come
decisions.reason: Readable says why the one coming was expected, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name, as in 7:13.

records.source: παραγενόμενοι δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς ἀπέστειλεν ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;
records.gloss: Having come then to him the men said, John the Baptist has sent us to you saying, You are the coming [one] or another should we wait for?
pieces: When the men reached {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they said, "John the Baptist sent us to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to ask, 'Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is to come, or are we to look for someone else?'"

L.20: And when the men had come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they said, "John the Baptist has sent us to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, saying, 'Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is coming, or should we wait for another?'"

R.20: The men came to Jesus and said, "John the Baptist sent us to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He wants to know, 'Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one God promised would come? Or should we keep waiting for someone else?'"

decisions.choice: the Baptist: the one who baptizes
alternatives: a member of a group called Baptists
decisions.reason: The title marks John by what he did (3:3). This is the first time Luke uses it (also 7:33; 9:19).

decisions.choice: the question repeated word for word
decisions.reason: Luke repeats John's question in full, which gives it weight.

decisions.choice: the one God promised would come
decisions.reason: As in 7:19.

records.source: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς ἀπὸ νόσων καὶ μαστίγων καὶ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν, καὶ τυφλοῖς πολλοῖς ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν.
records.gloss: In that the hour he healed many from diseases and afflictions and spirits evil, and to blind many he granted to see.
pieces: Just then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed many people of diseases, painful illnesses and evil spirits, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave many blind people the gift of sight.

L.21: In that hour {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed many of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and to many blind [people] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} granted sight.

R.21: At that very time Jesus was healing many people. Some had diseases or terrible pains, and some had evil spirits. Jesus also made many blind people able to see.

decisions.choice: afflictions: painful illnesses
decisions.reason: The word means a whip or a lash, and so a suffering that strikes like one (Mark 5:29, 34).

decisions.choice: granted: gave as a free gift
decisions.reason: The verb means to give freely, as a favor. It is used again in 7:42-43 of canceling a debt.

decisions.choice: in that hour: while John's messengers were there
decisions.reason: The healings take place before their eyes, so that they can tell John what they have seen (7:22).

decisions.choice: Jesus was healing
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and breaks the list into short sentences.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ εἴδετε καὶ ἠκούσατε· τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν, χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται, κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται, πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται·
records.gloss: And answering he said to them, Having gone report to John what you saw and heard: blind receive sight, lame walk, lepers are cleansed, deaf hear, dead are raised, poor have good news proclaimed;
pieces: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered them, "Go back and tell John what you have seen and heard. The blind see again, the lame walk, people with leprosy are made clean, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor hear the good news.

L.22: And answering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: blind [people] receive sight, lame [people] walk, lepers are cleansed, and deaf [people] hear, dead [people] are raised, poor [people] have good news proclaimed [to them];

R.22: Jesus answered John's followers, "Go back and tell John what you have seen and heard. Blind people can see. People who could not walk are walking. People with skin diseases are healed and made clean. Deaf people can hear. Dead people are raised to life. And poor people are hearing the good news.

decisions.choice: the list echoes Isaiah's promises of what God would do
decisions.reason: Isaiah promised that the blind would see, the deaf hear and the lame leap (Isaiah 35:5-6; 29:18), that the dead would live (Isaiah 26:19), and that good news would come to the poor (Isaiah 61:1, read by Jesus in 4:18). Jesus answers John's question with the deeds the prophets promised.

decisions.choice: lepers: people with a skin disease that made them unclean under the law
alternatives: people with the disease now called leprosy only
decisions.reason: As in 5:12, the word covered several skin diseases (Leviticus 13). Healing meant they could be declared clean and return to their community.

decisions.choice: the poor have good news proclaimed: the climax of the list
decisions.reason: The list ends with the poor, as in Jesus's reading of Isaiah (4:18). The verb is the one for telling good news (1:19; 3:18).

decisions.choice: people with skin diseases
decisions.reason: As in 5:12, Readable describes the disease instead of naming it.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:23
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer runs on into 7:23.

records.source: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.
records.gloss: And blessed is whoever not is caused to stumble in me.
pieces: And blessed is anyone who does not find in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a reason to fall away."

L.23: And blessed is whoever is not caused to stumble because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

R.23: How blessed is anyone who does not stumble and turn away because of what I do!"

decisions.choice: caused to stumble: tripped up, so as to turn away from Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a trap or a stumbling block. It means to be led to fall away, not just to feel hurt. Jesus does not fit what some expect (7:34), and they turn from him.

decisions.choice: blessed: fortunate in God's eyes
decisions.reason: The word is the one of the blessings in 6:20-22.

decisions.choice: because of what I do
decisions.reason: Readable links the saying to the deeds of 7:22, which did not look like the judgment John announced.

decisions.choice: How blessed is anyone
decisions.reason: Readable makes the declaration an exclamation, as in 6:20.

records.source: Ἀπελθόντων δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων Ἰωάννου ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς ὄχλους περὶ Ἰωάννου· Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι;
records.gloss: Having departed then the messengers of John he began to speak to the crowds concerning John, What did you go out into the wilderness to look at?
pieces: After John's messengers had gone, Jesus began to talk to the crowds about John. "What did you go out into the wilderness to see?

L.24: When John's messengers had left, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to speak to the crowds about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to look at?

R.24: When John's messengers had left, Jesus began to talk to the crowds about John. He said, "When you went out into the desert to see John, what did you expect to see?

decisions.choice: messengers: people sent with a message
decisions.reason: The word can mean angel, but here it is John's two disciples. Jesus will use the same word of John himself in 7:27.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: the dry country near the Jordan where John preached
decisions.reason: Crowds went out to hear John and be baptized (3:2-7).

decisions.choice: to look at: to gaze at, as at a sight
decisions.reason: The verb means to look closely at something worth seeing.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:28
decisions.reason: Jesus's words about John run on through 7:28.

decisions.choice: desert
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for dry, empty country.

records.heading: Jesus speaks about John

records.source: κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;
records.gloss: A reed by wind being shaken?
pieces: A reed swaying in the wind?

L.24: A reed being shaken by [the] wind?

R.24: A tall reed that the wind blows back and forth?

decisions.choice: a reed shaken by the wind: a weak, changeable person
alternatives: the actual reeds along the Jordan only
decisions.reason: Reeds grew thick along the Jordan, and people would have seen them. But a reed that bends with every wind is also a picture of weakness (1 Kings 14:15; 2 Kings 18:21). John was no such man; he spoke the same hard truth to everyone, even Herod (3:19).

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is ironic: no one went out to the wilderness to stare at reeds.

records.source: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν;
records.gloss: But what did you go out to see?
pieces: If not, what did you go out to see?

L.25: But what did you go out to see?

R.25: What else did you expect to see?

decisions.choice: but: if not that, then what?
decisions.reason: The word sets aside the answer just suggested and asks again.

records.source: ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἱματίοις ἠμφιεσμένον;
records.gloss: A man in soft garments having been dressed?
pieces: A man dressed in soft, fine clothes?

L.25: A man dressed in soft clothing?

R.25: A man wearing soft, expensive clothes?

decisions.choice: soft clothing: fine, costly clothing worn by the rich
decisions.reason: Soft cloth was a sign of wealth and an easy life. John wore clothing of camel's hair (Matthew 3:4).

records.source: ἰδοὺ οἱ ἐν ἱματισμῷ ἐνδόξῳ καὶ τρυφῇ ὑπάρχοντες ἐν τοῖς βασιλείοις εἰσίν.
records.gloss: Look, those in clothing splendid and in luxury living in the palaces are.
pieces: Those who wear splendid clothes and live in luxury are found in the palaces of kings.

L.25: Look, those who live in splendid clothing and luxury are in the royal palaces.

R.25: People who wear fine clothes and live in luxury are in the palaces of kings.

decisions.choice: palaces: the courts of kings, such as Herod's
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas had John imprisoned (3:19-20). The men of the palace dressed in fine clothes; the prophet of the wilderness was locked up by them.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

records.source: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν;
records.gloss: But what did you go out to see?
pieces: Then what did you go out to see?

L.26: But what did you go out to see?

R.26: So what did you go out to see?

decisions.choice: the question asked a third time
decisions.reason: The repeated question builds to the real answer.

records.source: προφήτην;
records.gloss: A prophet?
pieces: A prophet?

R.26: Did you go to see a prophet?

decisions.choice: a prophet: one who speaks God's message
alternatives: one who only predicts the future
decisions.reason: The people took John for a prophet (20:6). No prophet had arisen in Israel for a long time.

decisions.choice: Did you go to see
decisions.reason: Readable makes the question a full sentence.

records.source: ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.
records.gloss: Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.
pieces: Yes, I tell you, and far more than a prophet.

L.26: Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

R.26: Yes, he is a prophet. But I tell you, he is even more than a prophet.

decisions.choice: more than a prophet: greater in his task than all the prophets before him
decisions.reason: John is himself the messenger the prophets foretold, as the next verse shows (1:76).

decisions.choice: he is a prophet. But
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "yes" agrees with.

records.source: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.
records.gloss: This is [he] concerning whom it has been written, Look, I send the messenger of me before face of you, who will prepare the way of you before you.
pieces: He is the one of whom Scripture says, 'I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger to go before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; he will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} road ready ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

L.27: This is [the one] about whom it is written: 'Look, I send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, who will prepare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

R.27: John is the one the Scriptures speak about. There God says to the one who is to come, 'I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He will get the road ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

decisions.choice: Malachi 3:1, with words from Exodus 23:20
decisions.reason: In Malachi 3:1 God says, "I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me." The words "before your face" come from Exodus 23:20, where God sends his angel before Israel. Mark 1:2 and Matthew 11:10 quote the same words.

decisions.choice: you and your: God speaks to the one who is to come, that is, to Jesus
decisions.reason: In Malachi the messenger prepares the way before the LORD himself. In Luke's quotation God speaks to another, and the messenger prepares that one's way. So the coming of Jesus is the coming of the LORD that Malachi promised (compare 1:76; 3:4). This answers John's question of 7:19.

decisions.choice: my messenger: God is the speaker
decisions.reason: In Malachi the speaker is the LORD of hosts. John is the messenger God sends.

decisions.choice: messenger: the same word as in 7:24
decisions.reason: John sent messengers to Jesus; John himself is God's messenger.

decisions.choice: my (God speaking) and you, your (spoken to Jesus), with the capital-pronoun setting
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself, and he speaks to Jesus, so both take the capital-pronoun setting. "He" is the messenger, John, and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: There God says to the one who is to come
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and the one spoken to, as the meaning decisions explain.

decisions.choice: to go before you (B); before your face (L)
decisions.reason: "Before your face" is a Hebrew way of saying "ahead of you". Literal keeps it.

records.source: λέγω ὑμῖν, μείζων ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν Ἰωάννου οὐδείς ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.
records.gloss: I say to you, greater among born of women than John no one is; the but least in the kingdom of the God greater than him is.
pieces: I tell you, of all who have been born of women, there is none greater than John. Yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he is."

L.28: I tell you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; but the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."

R.28: I tell you, no one who has ever been born is greater than John. But even the least important person in the kingdom of God is greater than he is."

decisions.choice: among those born of women: among all human beings
alternatives: among the sons of mothers only
decisions.reason: The phrase is a Hebrew way of saying all people (Job 14:1).

decisions.choice: the least: the one of lowest rank
alternatives: the lesser one, meaning Jesus, who came after John
decisions.reason: The word is a comparative, "lesser", which here has the force of "least". Some readers in the early church took it to mean Jesus, younger than John and seen as lesser. But the contrast is between all who have lived and anyone in the kingdom of God.

decisions.choice: greater than John: not in character, but in what God has given
alternatives: John is shut out of the kingdom
decisions.reason: John stands at the turning point, the last and greatest of those who announced what was coming (16:16). To share in the kingdom that has now come with Jesus is a greater gift than even John's great task.

decisions.choice: no one who has ever been born
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here and opens again in 7:31
decisions.reason: 7:29-30 are the narrator's words, as the decision on 7:29 explains.

records.source: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν, βαπτισθέντες τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου·
records.gloss: And all the people having heard and the tax collectors declared righteous the God, having been baptized [with] the baptism of John;
pieces: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, agreed that God was in the right, because they had been baptized with John's baptism.

L.29: And all the people who heard, even the tax collectors, justified God, having been baptized with the baptism of John;

R.29: All the people who heard Jesus say this agreed that God's way was right. Even the tax collectors agreed. They were the ones who had let John baptize them.

decisions.choice: 7:29-30 are the narrator's comment, not part of Jesus's speech
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT does not use quotation marks, but it ends Jesus's words with a full stop at 7:28 and starts a new paragraph at 7:31, where Jesus asks another question. 7:29-30 tell, in the past tense, how two groups had responded to John, which is how Luke the narrator speaks (compare 3:10-14 and 20:4-7). Some read the verses as Jesus's own words; the meaning would not change.

decisions.choice: justified God: declared that God was right
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare someone in the right. The people acknowledged that God's way, shown in John's call to repent, was right. The same verb returns in 7:35.

decisions.choice: who heard: who heard Jesus's words about John
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. Jesus has just spoken about John to the crowds (7:24), and the people who had accepted John's baptism agreed.

decisions.choice: tax collectors: Jews who collected taxes for Rome or its rulers, and were despised
decisions.reason: As in 3:12 and 5:27-30, these were people others looked down on. They had come to John to be baptized (3:12).

decisions.choice: agreed that God was in the right (B); agreed that God's way was right (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "justifying" God means, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: heard Jesus say this
decisions.reason: Readable says what they heard, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς, μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: The but Pharisees and the lawyers the purpose of the God rejected for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
pieces: But the Pharisees and the experts in the law refused what God intended for them, since they had not let John baptize them.

L.30: But the Pharisees and the experts in the law set aside the purpose of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him.

R.30: But the Pharisees and the experts in God's law turned away from what God wanted to do for them. They would not let John baptize them.

decisions.choice: experts in the law: men trained in the law of Moses, much like the scribes
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for the experts who taught and applied God's law (10:25; 11:45-52). Many were Pharisees.

decisions.choice: the purpose of God: God's plan, here his call to repent through John
decisions.reason: The noun means a plan or decision. Luke uses it of God's saving plan (Acts 2:23; 20:27).

decisions.choice: for themselves: the plan was meant for them, and they rejected it
decisions.reason: The phrase can go with "rejected" (they rejected it, to their own loss) or with "purpose" (God's purpose for them). Either way they turned down what God offered them.

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a movement of Jews devoted to keeping God's law in every part of life
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17 and 6:2.

decisions.choice: experts in God's law (R); experts in the law (L, B)
decisions.reason: Today "lawyer" suggests courts and contracts. The word means someone expert in the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John, so the reader does not think of Jesus.

records.source: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι;
records.gloss: To what then will I liken the people of the generation this, and to what are they like?
pieces: Jesus went on, "Then how shall I picture the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation? What are they like?

L.31: "To what then shall I compare the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation, and what are they like?

R.31: Jesus continued, "How can I describe the {{gender:people|men}} who live today? What are they like?

decisions.choice: this generation: the people of Jesus's time, as a whole
alternatives: a period of thirty or forty years
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the people of his day who refused both John and himself (11:29-32; 17:25).

decisions.choice: two questions with one meaning
decisions.reason: The second question repeats the first, a Hebrew way of giving a saying weight.

decisions.choice: people: human beings, men and women
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: Jesus went on (B); Jesus continued (R)
decisions.reason: After the narrator's comment in 7:29-30, Balanced and Readable say that Jesus is speaking again. Literal only opens the quotation again.

decisions.choice: who live today
decisions.reason: Readable says what "generation" means here.

records.source: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις, ἃ λέγει· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε·
records.gloss: Like they are to children who in marketplace are sitting and calling to one another, which says, We played the flute for you and not you danced; we sang a lament and not you wept.
pieces: They are like small children who sit in the town square and shout to each other, 'We played wedding music on the flute for you, and you would not dance. We sang a funeral song, and you would not cry.'

L.32: They are like children sitting in [the] marketplace and calling to one another, who say, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not weep.'

R.32: They are like children sitting in the town square. They call out to each other, 'We played happy music on the flute for you, but you would not dance! We sang sad songs, but you would not cry!'

decisions.choice: the marketplace: the open square of a town, where people met and children played
decisions.reason: Every town had an open space for buying, selling and meeting.

decisions.choice: played the flute, sang a lament: children playing at weddings and at funerals
decisions.reason: Flute music went with weddings and feasts; wailing songs went with funerals. The children want the others to play their game, but the others will join in neither. So the people of this generation would accept neither John nor Jesus.

decisions.choice: which says: what the children call out
decisions.reason: The singular "says" goes with the neuter plural "children", as Greek allows.

decisions.choice: wedding music (B), happy music (R); a funeral song (B), sad songs (R)
alternatives: played the flute; sang a lament
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of game the children were playing, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς μὴ ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον, καὶ λέγετε· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·
records.gloss: Has come for John the Baptist not eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, A demon he has;
pieces: For John the Baptist has come eating no bread and drinking no wine, and you say, 'There is a demon in him.'

L.33: For John the Baptist has come not eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, 'He has a demon.'

R.33: John the Baptist came, and he went without bread and did not drink wine. And you said, 'He has a demon in him!'

decisions.choice: not eating bread nor drinking wine: John lived a strict life of fasting
decisions.reason: John was to drink no wine (1:15), and he lived in the wilderness on simple food (Matthew 3:4). His disciples fasted often (5:33).

decisions.choice: he has a demon: he is mad, driven by an evil spirit
decisions.reason: People said the same of Jesus (John 7:20; 10:20). It dismissed John as out of his mind.

decisions.choice: past tense: came, said
decisions.reason: Readable tells it as a story of what happened.

records.source: ἐλήλυθεν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐσθίων καὶ πίνων, καὶ λέγετε· Ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπος φάγος καὶ οἰνοπότης, φίλος τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν.
records.gloss: Has come the Son of the Man eating and drinking, and you say, Look, a man a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.
pieces: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look at the man! He is greedy for food and a heavy drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'

L.34: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, 'Look, a man who is a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'

R.34: The Son of Man came, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ate and drank. And you said, 'Look at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! He eats too much and drinks too much wine. He is a friend of tax collectors and sinners!'

decisions.choice: a glutton and a drunkard: the charge against a rebellious son in Deuteronomy 21:20
alternatives: a mere insult with no echo
decisions.reason: The law speaks of a stubborn son who is a glutton and a drunkard. The words brand Jesus as a disgrace to his people.

decisions.choice: a friend of tax collectors and sinners: one who shares meals with outcasts
alternatives: one who approves of their sins
decisions.reason: Jesus ate with tax collectors and sinners (5:29-32), and he will do so again (7:36-50; 15:1-2; 19:7).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's name for himself, as in 5:24 and 6:5
decisions.reason: Jesus contrasts John's fasting with his own way of life, which was open to everyone.

decisions.choice: greedy for food and a heavy drinker (B); eats too much and drinks too much wine (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for the old ones.

decisions.choice: Look (L); Look at the man (B); Look at him (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word points at Jesus with scorn, so Balanced and Readable keep it and say what is pointed at. "Behold" is old-fashioned.

records.source: καὶ ἐδικαιώθη ἡ σοφία ἀπὸ πάντων τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: And was justified the wisdom by all the children of her.
pieces: Yet wisdom is shown to be right by all who are her children."

L.35: And wisdom was justified by all her children."

R.35: But God's wisdom is shown to be right by all the people who accept it."

decisions.choice: wisdom: God's wisdom, seen in his plan through John and Jesus
decisions.reason: In Proverbs, wisdom is pictured as a woman who calls people to follow her (Proverbs 8:1-4; 9:1-6). Here she stands for God's wise plan, which sent John and Jesus in different ways (compare 11:49).

decisions.choice: her children: those who accept wisdom and live by it
decisions.reason: In Hebrew speech the children of something share its nature. The children of wisdom are the people who accepted God's call through John and Jesus, like the tax collectors of 7:29.

decisions.choice: was justified: was shown to be right
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 7:29: the people who accepted John's baptism declared God right. The tense is a timeless past: wisdom has been proved right every time.

decisions.choice: is shown to be right
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the verb means here, and use the present, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: God's wisdom; the people who accept it
decisions.reason: Readable names whose wisdom it is and explains "her children".

records.source: Ἠρώτα δέ τις αὐτὸν τῶν Φαρισαίων ἵνα φάγῃ μετ’ αὐτοῦ· καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ Φαρισαίου κατεκλίθη.
records.gloss: Was asking then one of him of the Pharisees that he would eat with him; and having entered into the house of the Pharisee he reclined.
pieces: One of the Pharisees invited Jesus to a meal with him. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into the Pharisee's house and took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} place at the table.

L.36: Now one of the Pharisees was asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to eat with him, and entering into the Pharisee's house, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reclined [at table].

R.36: A Pharisee invited Jesus to come and eat with him. So Jesus went to the Pharisee's house and lay down on a couch at the table, as people did for a dinner.

decisions.choice: reclined: lay on a couch at the table, leaning on one elbow
decisions.reason: At a formal meal guests lay on couches around a low table, with their feet away from it. This is why the woman could stand behind Jesus at his feet (7:38).

decisions.choice: a Pharisee's invitation: Jesus ate with Pharisees as well as with sinners
decisions.reason: Luke tells of three meals with Pharisees (7:36; 11:37; 14:1). Jesus has just been called a friend of sinners (7:34).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: lay down on a couch at the table, as people did for a dinner
decisions.reason: Readable explains the custom, which the next verses need.

records.heading: The woman with the alabaster flask

records.source: καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ ἥτις ἦν ἐν τῇ πόλει ἁμαρτωλός, καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα ὅτι κατάκειται ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ τοῦ Φαρισαίου, κομίσασα ἀλάβαστρον μύρου καὶ στᾶσα ὀπίσω παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ κλαίουσα, τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἤρξατο βρέχειν τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς ἐξέμασσεν, καὶ κατεφίλει τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ καὶ ἤλειφεν τῷ μύρῳ.
records.gloss: And look a woman who was in the city a sinner, and having learned that he is reclining in the house of the Pharisee, having brought an alabaster flask of perfume \v 38 and having stood behind at the feet of him weeping, with the tears she began to wet the feet of him and with the hairs of the head of her she was wiping, and was kissing the feet of him and was anointing with the perfume.
pieces: Now there was a woman in the town who was a sinner. When she found out that Jesus was at table in the Pharisee's house, she came with an alabaster flask of perfume.

She stood behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, crying, and began to wet {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with her tears. She dried them with the hair of her head, and she kissed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet over and over and anointed them with the perfume.

L.37: And look, a woman in the town who was a sinner, learning that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was reclining [at table] in the Pharisee's house, brought an alabaster flask of perfume,
L.38: and standing behind at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, weeping, she began to wet {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with [her] tears, and she was wiping [them] with the hair of her head, and she was kissing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and anointing [them] with the perfume.

R.37: In that town there was a woman everyone knew as a sinner. She heard that Jesus was eating at the Pharisee's house. So she came, carrying a beautiful stone jar full of expensive perfume.
R.38: She stood behind Jesus at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, and she was crying. Her tears fell on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet and made them wet. Then she dried {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet with her hair. She kept kissing them and pouring the perfume on them.

decisions.choice: a sinner: a woman known in the town for an immoral life
alternatives: a woman who had committed some private sin
decisions.reason: The word marks someone whose way of life openly broke God's law (5:30). Luke does not say what her sin was. Later tradition made her Mary Magdalene, but Luke introduces Mary Magdalene in the next chapter as a different person (8:2).

decisions.choice: an alabaster flask of perfume: a sealed jar of soft stone holding costly perfumed oil
decisions.reason: Alabaster was a smooth, pale stone used for jars of precious perfume. The perfume was far more costly than the olive oil of 7:46.

decisions.choice: wiping his feet with her hair: an act of humble devotion, unusual in public
decisions.reason: A respectable woman did not let down her hair in front of men. She uses her own hair and tears where the host had given no water (7:44).

decisions.choice: this is not the anointing at Bethany
alternatives: the same event as Mark 14:3-9 and John 12:1-8
decisions.reason: Those Gospels tell of a woman who anointed Jesus at Bethany, near Jerusalem, in the last week of his life. Luke's story takes place in Galilee, in a Pharisee's house, much earlier. Luke does not tell the Bethany anointing.

decisions.choice: began to wet, was kissing, was anointing: actions continued over time
decisions.reason: The tenses describe what she kept on doing. Jesus says she has not stopped kissing his feet (7:45).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: a beautiful stone jar
decisions.reason: Readable describes alabaster instead of naming it.

decisions.choice: anointed (B); pouring the perfume on (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what anointing the feet meant.

records.source: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Φαρισαῖος ὁ καλέσας αὐτὸν εἶπεν ἐν ἑαυτῷ λέγων· Οὗτος εἰ ἦν προφήτης, ἐγίνωσκεν ἂν τίς καὶ ποταπὴ ἡ γυνὴ ἥτις ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἁμαρτωλός ἐστιν.
records.gloss: Having seen then the Pharisee the [one] having invited him spoke within himself saying, This [man] if he were a prophet, would know who and what kind the woman who is touching him, that a sinner she is.
pieces: The Pharisee who had invited {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw this and said to himself, "This man, if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were a prophet, would have known who this woman is who is touching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and what sort of woman she is: a sinner."

L.39: Now when the Pharisee who had invited {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw [this], he spoke within himself, saying, "This man, if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were a prophet, would know who and what sort of woman [this is] who is touching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, that she is a sinner."

R.39: The Pharisee who had invited Jesus saw what was happening. He thought, "This man cannot be a prophet. A prophet would know who this woman is, the one touching {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He would know what kind of woman she is. She is a sinner!"

decisions.choice: if he were a prophet, he would know: the Pharisee assumes that Jesus is not a prophet
alternatives: a real question whether he is
decisions.reason: The form of the sentence states something contrary to fact: he would know, but he does not, so he is no prophet. Jesus answers by reading the Pharisee's own unspoken thoughts (7:40).

decisions.choice: a prophet, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: the prophet, the reading of some early manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few early manuscripts have "the prophet", meaning the prophet like Moses promised in Deuteronomy 18:15. Most have "a prophet". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: touching: the touch of a sinner would make him unclean, in the Pharisee's eyes
decisions.reason: The Pharisees took great care to avoid what made them unclean. The host thinks Jesus should have known and drawn back.

decisions.choice: spoke within himself: thought to himself, without speaking aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase means private thought (3:8; 12:17).

decisions.choice: This man cannot be a prophet. A prophet would know
alternatives: if he were a prophet, he would know
decisions.reason: Readable states the conclusion the condition implies, as the meaning decision explains, and then gives the reasoning.

records.source: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν· Σίμων, ἔχω σοί τι εἰπεῖν.
records.gloss: And answering Jesus said to him, Simon, I have to you something to say.
pieces: Jesus answered him, "Simon, there is something I want to tell you."

L.40: And answering, Jesus said to him, "Simon, I have something to say to you."

R.40: Jesus answered the Pharisee's thoughts. He said, "Simon, I have something to tell you."

decisions.choice: answering: Jesus answers what the Pharisee only thought
decisions.reason: The host spoke only within himself (7:39). Jesus answers him, which shows that he is indeed a prophet who knows hearts (5:22; 6:8).

decisions.choice: Simon: the Pharisee's name
decisions.reason: Simon was a common name. This Simon is the Pharisee who invited Jesus, not the disciple Simon Peter.

decisions.choice: answered the Pharisee's thoughts
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus answered, as the meaning decision explains.

records.source: ὁ δέ· Διδάσκαλε, εἰπέ, φησίν.
records.gloss: And he: Teacher, say [it], he says.
pieces: "Say it, Teacher," he replied.

decisions.choice: Teacher: a respectful title for a teacher of the law
decisions.reason: Simon gives Jesus the title of a respected teacher (3:12), not more.

decisions.choice: he says: a present tense in the story
decisions.reason: Greek often tells a past event in the present for vividness.

decisions.choice: replied (B); said (R)
decisions.reason: English tells the story in the past.

records.source: δύο χρεοφειλέται ἦσαν δανιστῇ τινι· ὁ εἷς ὤφειλεν δηνάρια πεντακόσια, ὁ δὲ ἕτερος πεντήκοντα.
records.gloss: Two debtors were to a moneylender certain; the one owed denarii five hundred, the and other fifty.
pieces: Jesus said, "A moneylender had two men who owed him money. One owed him 500 denarii, and the other fifty.

L.41: "Two debtors belonged to a certain moneylender; the one owed 500 denarii, and the other fifty.

R.41: Jesus said, "Two men owed money to a man who lent money. One of them owed him 500 silver coins. The other owed him fifty.

decisions.choice: denarii: Roman silver coins, each the usual pay for a day's work
decisions.reason: A denarius was a laborer's wage for a day (Matthew 20:2). So 500 denarii was more than a year's wages, and fifty about two months' wages. Both were real debts; one was ten times the other.

decisions.choice: a story told to answer Simon's thoughts
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the unspoken charge of 7:39 with a short parable.

decisions.choice: Jesus said
decisions.reason: The Greek starts the story without a new speech verb. Balanced and Readable name the speaker after Simon's reply; Literal only opens the quotation.

decisions.choice: silver coins (R); denarii (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable describes the coin instead of naming it. A modern sum would be misleading, since wages differ from place to place; the meaning decision gives the coin's worth.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:42
decisions.reason: The parable and its question are one speech.

records.source: μὴ ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι ἀμφοτέροις ἐχαρίσατο.
records.gloss: Not having they to repay, both he forgave.
pieces: Neither of them could pay him back, so he freely canceled the debts of both.

L.42: When they did not have [the means] to repay, he freely forgave [them] both.

R.42: Neither of them had the money to pay him back. So he kindly canceled what both of them owed.

decisions.choice: forgave: canceled the debt as a free gift
decisions.reason: The verb means to give freely, as a favor (7:21). The debts are wiped out, not put off. The word prepares for the forgiveness of sins in 7:47-48.

decisions.choice: the debts of both (B); what both of them owed (R)
decisions.reason: English needs to say what was forgiven.

records.source: τίς οὖν αὐτῶν πλεῖον ἀγαπήσει αὐτόν;
records.gloss: Which then of them more will love him?
pieces: So which of the two will love him more?"

L.42: Which of them, then, will love him more?"

R.42: Which of these two men will love the moneylender more?"

decisions.choice: love: grateful love toward the one who forgave
decisions.reason: In the story, love is the response of the one forgiven. The point is applied in 7:47.

decisions.choice: the moneylender
decisions.reason: Readable names the person, so that "him" is clear.

records.source: ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ὑπολαμβάνω ὅτι ᾧ τὸ πλεῖον ἐχαρίσατο.
records.gloss: Answering Simon said, I suppose that [the one] to whom the more he forgave.
pieces: Simon answered, "I would think the one whose larger debt he canceled."

L.43: Simon answered and said, "I suppose [the one] to whom he forgave the more."

R.43: Simon answered, "I think it is the man who owed more and was forgiven more."

decisions.choice: I suppose: I take it, a cautious answer
decisions.reason: Simon gives the obvious answer, perhaps reluctantly, sensing where the story is going.

decisions.choice: larger debt (B); owed more (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the more" refers to.

records.source: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ὀρθῶς ἔκρινας.
records.gloss: And he said to him, Rightly you have judged.
pieces: Jesus said to him, "Your judgment is right."

L.43: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "You have judged rightly."

decisions.choice: you have judged: you have given a right verdict
decisions.reason: The verb means to decide or give a verdict. Simon has judged rightly in the story, and now must apply it to himself.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

records.source: καὶ στραφεὶς πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα τῷ Σίμωνι ἔφη· Βλέπεις ταύτην τὴν γυναῖκα;
records.gloss: And having turned toward the woman to Simon he said, You see this the woman?
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned toward the woman and said to Simon, "Do you see this woman?

L.44: And turning toward the woman, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Simon, "Do you see this woman?

R.44: Then Jesus turned toward the woman. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to Simon: "Do you see this woman?

decisions.choice: turning to the woman, he spoke to Simon: Jesus looks at her while he speaks to him
decisions.reason: Jesus turns Simon's eyes to the woman he has judged.

decisions.choice: do you see this woman: do you see her as she really is
decisions.reason: Simon has seen only a sinner (7:39). Jesus asks him to look again.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:47
decisions.reason: Jesus's words to Simon run on through 7:47.

records.source: εἰσῆλθόν σου εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, ὕδωρ μοι ἐπὶ πόδας οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ τοῖς δάκρυσιν ἔβρεξέν μου τοὺς πόδας καὶ ταῖς θριξὶν αὐτῆς ἐξέμαξεν.
records.gloss: I entered of you into the house, water to me for feet not you gave; she but with the tears wet of me the feet and with the hairs of her wiped [them].
pieces: When I came into your house, you gave {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} no water to wash {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. But she has made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet wet with her tears and dried them with her hair.

L.44: I entered into your house; you did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} water for [{{deity_pronoun:my|My}}] feet, but she has wet {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet with [her] tears and wiped [them] with her hair.

R.44: I came into your house, and you did not even give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} water to wash {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet. But this woman has washed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet with her tears and dried them with her hair.

decisions.choice: water for my feet: a common courtesy to a guest who had walked on dusty roads
alternatives: a legal duty of the host
decisions.reason: Hosts offered guests water to wash their feet (Genesis 18:4; 24:32; Judges 19:21). Simon did not; Luke does not say whether he meant to insult Jesus.

decisions.choice: she: set in sharp contrast with Simon
decisions.reason: In 7:44-46 each thing Simon did not do is set against what the woman did, in three pairs.

decisions.choice: to wash my feet
decisions.reason: English says what the water was for.

decisions.choice: washed
decisions.reason: Readable carries the contrast with the water Simon did not give.

records.source: φίλημά μοι οὐκ ἔδωκας· αὕτη δὲ ἀφ’ ἧς εἰσῆλθον οὐ διέλιπεν καταφιλοῦσά μου τοὺς πόδας.
records.gloss: A kiss to me not you gave; she but from which I came in not has stopped kissing of me the feet.
pieces: You did not welcome {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with a kiss. But ever since I came in, she has kept on kissing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet.

L.45: You did not give {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a kiss; but she, from the time I came in, has not stopped kissing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet.

R.45: You did not greet {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} with a kiss. But from the time I came in, she has not stopped kissing {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet.

decisions.choice: a kiss: the usual greeting of welcome
decisions.reason: A host greeted an honored guest with a kiss on the cheek (15:20; 22:47-48).

decisions.choice: I came in, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: she came in, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "she came in". The SBLGNT reading means she has been kissing his feet as long as he has been there. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

records.source: ἐλαίῳ τὴν κεφαλήν μου οὐκ ἤλειψας· αὕτη δὲ μύρῳ ἤλειψεν τοὺς πόδας μου.
records.gloss: With oil the head of me not you anointed; she but with perfume anointed the feet of me.
pieces: You did not anoint {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head with olive oil, but she has anointed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet with costly perfume.

L.46: You did not anoint {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head with oil; but she has anointed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet with perfume.

R.46: You did not put any olive oil on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} head. But she has rubbed expensive perfume on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feet.

decisions.choice: anointing the head with oil: a sign of welcome and honor to a guest
decisions.reason: Olive oil on the head refreshed a guest and honored him (Psalm 23:5; 141:5).

decisions.choice: oil and perfume: common olive oil set against costly perfume
alternatives: two words for the same oil
decisions.reason: Simon did not give even ordinary oil for the head; she gave precious perfume, and for the feet.

decisions.choice: olive oil; costly (B) or expensive (R) perfume
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the contrast between the two oils plain.

records.source: οὗ χάριν, λέγω σοι, ἀφέωνται αἱ ἁμαρτίαι αὐτῆς αἱ πολλαί, ὅτι ἠγάπησεν πολύ· ᾧ δὲ ὀλίγον ἀφίεται, ὀλίγον ἀγαπᾷ.
records.gloss: Of which for the sake, I say to you, have been forgiven the sins of her the many, because she loved much; to whom but little is forgiven, little he loves.
pieces: So I tell you, her sins, many as they are, stand forgiven; that is why she has shown so much love. But someone who is forgiven little loves little."

L.47: Therefore, I tell you, her sins, which are many, have been forgiven, for she loved much; but the one to whom little is forgiven loves little."

R.47: So I tell you, her many sins are forgiven, and that is why she has shown so much love. But a person who has been forgiven only a little loves only a little."

decisions.choice: for she loved much: her love shows that she has been forgiven; it is not the price of her forgiveness
alternatives: she is forgiven because she loved much
decisions.reason: The word "for" can give the reason for a fact or the reason we know it. The parable (7:41-43) makes love the result of forgiveness, and the end of the verse says the same: the one forgiven little loves little. In 7:50 Jesus says it was her faith that saved her. Her love is the evidence of a forgiveness she had already received.

decisions.choice: have been forgiven: forgiven, and that stands; God is the one who forgives
alternatives: forgiven at this moment for the first time
decisions.reason: The perfect tense describes a forgiveness that holds, as in 5:20.

decisions.choice: the one forgiven little: a general saying aimed at Simon
alternatives: a statement that Simon has few sins
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say Simon has little to be forgiven. He leaves Simon to see himself in the debtor who loves little.

decisions.choice: that is why she has shown so much love
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how her love relates to her forgiveness, as the meaning decision explains. A reader could take "because she loved much" to mean she earned it.

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῇ· Ἀφέωνταί σου αἱ ἁμαρτίαι.
records.gloss: He said then to her, Have been forgiven of you the sins.
pieces: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "Your sins stand forgiven."

L.48: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "Your sins have been forgiven."

R.48: Then Jesus said to the woman, "God has forgiven your sins."

decisions.choice: have been forgiven: as in 5:20, a forgiveness that stands, given by God
alternatives: Jesus forgives her now for the first time
decisions.reason: Jesus declares to her what he has just said about her (7:47). The passive leaves God as the one who forgives, which is why the guests ask who Jesus is (7:49).

decisions.choice: God has forgiven
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as in 5:20.

records.source: καὶ ἤρξαντο οἱ συνανακείμενοι λέγειν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Τίς οὗτός ἐστιν ὃς καὶ ἁμαρτίας ἀφίησιν;
records.gloss: And began those reclining with [him] to say within themselves, Who this is who even sins forgives?
pieces: The others at the table with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} began to say to one another, "Who is this man, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} even forgives sins?"

L.49: And those reclining [at table] with [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] began to say among themselves, "Who is this, who even forgives sins?"

R.49: The other guests began to ask each other, "Who is this man? He even forgives sins!"

decisions.choice: among themselves: to one another, or in their own minds
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean either, as in 7:39. Either way they do not ask Jesus.

decisions.choice: who is this: the guests see that he claims to do what only God does
decisions.reason: Only God forgives sins, as the scribes said in 5:21. The question who Jesus is runs through these chapters (5:21; 7:16, 19-20; 9:9, 18-20).

records.source: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τὴν γυναῖκα· Ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε· πορεύου εἰς εἰρήνην.
records.gloss: He said then to the woman, The faith of you has saved you; go into peace.
pieces: But Jesus said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you. Go in peace."

L.50: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you; go in peace."

R.50: Jesus said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you. Go home now, and have peace."

decisions.choice: faith: her trust in Jesus, shown in what she did
decisions.reason: Her tears and her coming to Jesus showed that she trusted him to receive her. Jesus says it was faith, not her love, that saved her (compare 7:47).

decisions.choice: has saved: rescued from sin and its judgment, and restored to God
decisions.reason: The same words are said to people Jesus heals (8:48; 17:19; 18:42). Here no sickness is mentioned: the salvation is the forgiveness of her sins (1:77).

decisions.choice: go in peace: a farewell blessing, here with its full meaning of peace with God
decisions.reason: The words were a usual farewell (1 Samuel 1:17). For the woman they mean she leaves forgiven and whole (8:48).

decisions.choice: Go home now, and have peace
decisions.reason: Readable makes the farewell plain and keeps the key word peace.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.
